ios.desc:
Your apps unlock when you move. Pick the apps that eat your time, set a goal like 8,000 steps or 20 push-ups, and Fitlock keeps them locked until you've done it.

Prefer a reward? Switch to Earn, and every walk, workout or set of squats earns you more screen time. Either way, you move more and scroll less.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Choose the apps to lock: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, games, whole categories or websites.
2. Pick a goal: steps, a run, a ride, a workout, push-ups counted by your camera, or just getting to the gym.
3. Choose how it pays off. Unlock: hit your goal and your apps open for the rest of the day. Earn: build up screen time as you move.
4. Get moving. Fitlock follows your progress through Apple Health and opens your apps the moment you've earned them.

NEW: INSIGHTS, STREAKS AND HOLIDAYS

• Insights shows how moving more shrinks your screen time, by day, week or month
• Every Monday, get a story of your week to look back on and share
• Spot your patterns, like the day you move most, and see how far you've come since you joined
• Keep your screen time history for good, not just the four weeks Apple keeps
• Every schedule builds a streak, with milestones to celebrate as it grows
• Need a day off? Take a holiday and your streak stays safe

MOVE YOUR WAY

• Steps, walking and running, cycling, workouts and meditation
• Wheelchair pushes and distance
• Push-ups and squats, counted by your iPhone's camera from any angle. No wearable needed
• Location goals: unlock your apps when you reach the gym, the office or the park
• Wearing an Apple Watch? Calories, exercise and stand minutes, time outside and swimming count too
• Workouts from apps like Strava, Peloton or Garmin count as well, once they're in Apple Health

STAY IN CONTROL

• Schedules for the times that matter: mornings, evenings, work hours, even overnight
• A starting allowance, like 30 minutes of Instagram, before the lock kicks in
• Short breaks for when you really need one
• Block a few apps, or everything except the ones you choose
• Choose how firm Fitlock is, up to Strict mode, which stops you editing a schedule while it runs
• Block App Store purchases and adult websites too
• Home Screen widgets show your progress at a glance

YOUR QUESTIONS

Do I need an Apple Watch?
No. Your iPhone counts your steps and your camera counts your reps. A Watch just adds more goals.

What if I really need an app?
Take a short break whenever you need one, or give yourself a starting allowance each day

quotes.text:
Hey all!

I noticed the amazing feedback touch grass received a couple of days ago, so thought I'd share my app here too.

Fitlock works with Apple Health to block apps behind daily health/fitness goals. Such as, step count, outside time, workout time, cycling, swimming, meditation and many more.

I would love to get your thoughts!
